title: financial literacy — monetary calculations, including making change with amounts to 1000 dollars and developing simple financial plans

lesson.title: Money Smarts: Making Change and Making a Plan

steps.say: Hi friend, it's Ms. Yuanyuan! Imagine you walk into a shop in Victoria with your saved-up money. A bike helmet costs thirteen dollars and forty-five cents, and you hand the cashier a twenty dollar bill. The cashier has to figure out how much money to give back to you. That money coming back is called the change. If nobody knew how to work out change, we would all be losing money every single day! So today we'll learn two money skills: making change, and making a simple money plan.

visual.caption: Prices at the shop, written in dollars and cents

steps.say: Here's the big secret about change. Change is just the gap between the price and the money you handed over. So we can find it by counting up from the price until we reach what we paid. From thirteen dollars and forty-five cents, we hop up the number line until we land on twenty dollars. That hop is six dollars and fifty-five cents. So the change is six dollars and fifty-five cents.

visual.caption: The jump from the price up to what we paid IS the change

steps.say: Let's slow that hop down, because counting up works best in friendly little steps. First hop up five cents, to get to thirteen dollars and fifty cents. Then hop up fifty cents, to reach fourteen dollars. Then one big hop of six dollars, to land on twenty dollars. Now add the hops: five cents plus fifty cents is fifty-five cents, plus six dollars makes six dollars and fifty-five cents. Same answer! And here's how we check: thirteen dollars forty-five plus six dollars fifty-five equals exactly twenty dollars.

visual.caption: Three friendly hops that add up to $6.55

steps.say: Now let's use bigger money, all the way up to one thousand dollars. Say a mountain bike at the shop costs three hundred forty-eight dollars and seventy-five cents, and your family pays with four one-hundred dollar bills, which is four hundred dollars. Count up again! Twenty-five cents gets you to three hundred forty-nine dollars. One dollar gets you to three hundred fifty. Then fifty dollars gets you to four hundred. Add the hops: twenty-five cents plus one dollar plus fifty dollars equals fifty-one dollars and twenty-five cents. Check it: three hundred forty-eight seventy-five plus fifty-one twenty-five equals four hundred dollars exactly.

visual.caption: Big money works exactly the same way — just count up

steps.say: Sometimes you buy a few things at once, so first you need the total. You grab a soccer ball for twenty-four dollars and ninety-nine cents, a water bottle for twelve dollars and fifty cents, and shin pads for eighteen dollars and twenty-five cents. Add them step by step: twenty-four ninety-nine plus twelve fifty is thirty-seven dollars and forty-nine cents. Then thirty-seven forty-nine plus eighteen twenty-five is fifty-five dollars and seventy-four cents. You pay with three twenty dollar bills, which is sixty dollars. Counting up from fifty-five seventy-four to sixty dollars gives four dollars and twenty-six cents change.

visual.caption: Three bars joined together make the total of $55.74

steps.say: Now the second money skill: making a plan. A plan starts with a budget. A budget just means the money coming in, and the money going out. Each month you get forty dollars allowance and earn thirty-five dollars walking your neighbour's dog, so your income is seventy-five dollars. You spend twelve dollars on snacks and eighteen dollars on comics, so your expenses are thirty dollars. Seventy-five dollars minus thirty dollars leaves forty-five dollars. That forty-five dollars is what you can save every month.

visual.caption: Income minus expenses equals what you get to save

steps.say: Last piece! Your goal is a bike that costs two hundred twenty-five dollars. You save forty-five dollars each month, so how long will it take? Just keep adding forty-five: after one month forty-five, two months ninety, three months one hundred thirty-five, four months one hundred eighty, five months two hundred twenty-five. That's the goal! Or you can divide: two hundred twenty-five divided by forty-five equals five. Five months of sticking to your plan, and the bike is yours.

visual.caption: Savings climbing month by month up to the $225 goal

steps.say: So remember this, my friend: to find change, count up from the price to what you paid. To reach a goal, take your income, subtract your expenses, and save the rest. You are officially money smart!

lesson.answer: Change is the count-up from the price to what you paid — and income minus expenses is what you can save toward your goal.

practice.question: At a shop in Kamloops, a raincoat costs $86.75 and you pay with a one hundred dollar bill. How much change do you get? Then, if you save $15 a week, how many weeks until you have saved $90?
practice.answer: Change is $13.25 (count up: 25 cents to $87, then $13 to $100; check $86.75 + $13.25 = $100). And $90 divided by $15 is 6 weeks.
